'''Payton A. Sandfort''' (born July 12, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]], and has played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].

==Early life==
Sandfort grew up in [[Waukee, Iowa]] and attended [[Waukee High School]], where he played basketball and golf. He averaged 19.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, and four assists as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2020/10/01/waukee-wing-payton-sandfort-prospect-analysis-iowa-basketball-fran-mccaffery-uthoff-wieskamp/5880344002/|title=How Waukee wing Payton Sandfort will fit with Iowa basketball|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=October 1, 2020|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref> Sandfort was named the Iowa Basketball Coaches Association 4A Player of the Year after averaging 16.6 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 3.1 assists during his senior season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Hawkeyes-Basketball-Payton-Sandfort-Carve-Out-Role-Freshman-Big-Ten-Conference-Basketball-Fran-McCaffery-166306776/|title=Payton Sandfort looking to carve out a role as a freshman: "It's really up to me"|first=Sean|last=Bock|website=[[247Sports]]|date=June 8, 2021|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref> He also helped Waukee to a state championship in golf as a senior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Hawkeyes-Basketball-Recruiting-Payton-Sandfort-Waukee-Golf-State-Championship-152824843/|title=Iowa hoops commit Sandfort leads Waukee golf to state title|first=Sean|last=Bock|website=[[247Sports]]|date=October 11, 2020|access-date=November 8, 2022}}</ref> Sandfort was rated a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] over offers from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Drake Bulldogs men's basketball|Drake]], [[Air Force Falcons men's basketball|Air Force]], and [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola Chicago]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/waukees-payton-sandfort-commits-to-iowa-mens-basketball-program/|title=Waukee's Payton Sandfort commits to Iowa men's basketball program|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]|date=October 2, 2020|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://iowa.rivals.com/news/payton-sandfort-commits-to-the-hawkeyes|title=Payton Sandfort commits to the Hawkeyes|first=Blair|last=Sanderson|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=October 1, 2020|access-date=November 8, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
Sandfort served as a role player off of the bench for the Iowa Hawkeyes as a freshman.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://qctimes.com/sandfort-becoming-more-productive-as-he-gets-comfortable/article_1c130f16-d692-50b1-b3da-ed38759073d6.html|title=Sandfort becoming more productive as he gets comfortable|work=[[Quad-City Times]]|date=November 22, 2021|access-date=November 8, 2022}}</ref> He played in 34 games and finished the season averaging five points and 1.9 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/basketball/payton-sandfort-growing-in-iowa-program|title=Payton Sandfort Growing in Iowa Program|first=John|last=Bohnenkamp|website=[[SI.com]]|date=June 17, 2022|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Payton-Sandfort-Iowa-Hawkeyes-Basketball-Ready-To-Show-More-Than-A-Shooter-In-Year-Two-194839437/|title='It's going to be more of a complete game': Payton Sandfort to show he's more than just a shooter in year two|first=Sean|last=Bock|website=[[247Sports]]|date=August 6, 2022|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref> Sandfort grew one inch between his freshman and sophomore years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://qctimes.com/sports/college/basketball/summer-a-season-of-growth-for-hawkeyes-sandfort/article_b7421a2e-61e3-556a-9dec-02ea789c6173.html|title=Summer a season of growth for Hawkeyes' Sandfort|work=[[Quad-City Times]]|access-date=November 8, 2022}}</ref> He entered his sophomore season as the Hawkeyes' starting shooting guard.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://qctimes.com/sports/watch-now-hawkeye-g-payton-sandfort-on-his-defense-in-iowas-season-opening-win/video_9e77aa0b-6ece-54af-8cc4-99ca33332d0b.html|title=Hawkeye G Payton Sandfort on his defense in Iowa's season-opening win|work=[[Quad-City Times]]|date=November 7, 2022|access-date=November 8, 2022}}</ref> Sandfort was moved to the bench due to poor shooting. At the end of the regular season, he was named the [[Big Ten Conference]] Sixth Man of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Basketball-Payton-Sandfort-named-Big-Tens-Sixth-Man-of-the-Year-205919593/|title=Iowa Basketball: Payton Sandfort named Big Ten's Sixth Man of the Year|first=David|last=Eikholt|website=[[247Sports]]|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}}</ref>

Sandfort averaged averaged 16.4 points, 6.6 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game as a junior, while shooting 44.6 percent from the field. He was named third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]]. He declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] before opting to return to Iowa.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bohnenkamp |first1=John |title=Payton Sandfort Trusts Gut in Big Decision |url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/basketball/payton-sandfort-trusts-gut-in-big-decision-01hz5x48zvae |access-date=December 19, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=May 30, 2024}}</ref> As a senior, Sandfort averaged 16.7 points, 6.0 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kulha |first1=Andrew |title=Former Iowa Star Payton Sandfort Explains His Fit With Oklahoma City Thunder |url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/basketball/former-iowa-hawkeyes-star-payton-sandfort-fit-oklahoma-city-thunder-nba |access-date=December 19, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=July 1, 2025}}</ref> He finished his Iowa career with 1,619 points, 622 rebounds and 256 assists.<ref name="tachman">{{cite news |last1=Tachman |first1=Tyler |title=Iowa basketball's Payton Sandfort agrees to deal with Oklahoma City Thunder |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2025/06/27/iowa-basketball-payton-sandfort-oklahoma-city-thunder-nba-hawkeyes/84359242007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-epti=z115353p001250c001250d00----v115353d--53--b--53--&gca-ft=196&gca-ds=sophi |access-date=December 19, 2025 |work=Hawk Central |date=June 27, 2025}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After not being selected in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Sandfort signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref name="tachman" /> He was waived on October 13, 2025, in order to join their G League affiliate the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hlas |first1=Mike |title=Former Iowa player Payton Sandfort joins Oklahoma City Thunder roster … for a day |url=https://www.thegazette.com/iowa-basketball/former-iowa-player-payton-sandfort-joins-oklahoma-city-thunder-roster-for-now/ |access-date=December 19, 2025 |work=The Gazette |date=October 13, 2025}}</ref> On March 2, 2026, Sandfort signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Thunder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder sign Payton Sandfort to two-way deal, waive Boeheim|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48082672/thunder-sign-payton-sandfort-two-way-contract-waive-buddy-boeheim|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On April 12, Sandfort recorded a career-high 23 points with five three-pointers during a 103–135 loss to the [[2025–26 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder's Payton Sandfort: Tallies 23 points off bench|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-payton-sandfort-tallies-23-points-off-bench/|access-date=April 26, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> He made four appearances for the Thunder during his rookie campaign, posting averages of 8.8 points and 2.5 rebounds. On July 2, Sandfort was waived by Oklahoma City.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OKC Thunder Waive Two-Way Swingman Payton Sandfort|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/onsi/okc-thunder-waive-two-way-swingman-payton-sandfort-01kwj2mx72ha|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sandfort's younger brother, [[Pryce Sandfort|Pryce]], plays basketball at [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/02/10/pryce-sandfort-recruiting-iowa-basketball-drake-washington-state-waukee-northwest/6703485001/|title=How Pryce Sandfort became Iowa boys basketball's most dominant scorer|work=[[The Des Moines Register]]|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=October 25, 2022}}</ref> His mother Gretchen played basketball at [[Simpson College]]. His father Brian played basketball at [[Hastings College]].

On August 15, 2026 he married his college sweetheart, Brooklyn McKee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcGlWByMueF/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref>
